JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.
2. Brief case of the petitioner in the nutshell:

It is the case of the petitioners that, on 11.05.2023 at about 6.45 p.m., when the deceased Thippeswamy was proceeding as passenger in private bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-19-AD-5259, on NH- 69, i.e. on Shivamogga to Sagar road, near Kumadwathi bridge, Shivamogga, at that time, the driver of the said bus drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against another bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-B-3076 which was coming from opposite direction and caused the accident.
Consequently, inmates of both the buses have sustained severe injuries and the deceased and the driver of the said bus have died on the spot.
Thereafter, dead body of the deceased was taken to Mc Gann hospital, Shivamogga wherein postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members.
The petitioners have spent huge amount towards Conveyance, Death Ceremony, Obsequies and etc. of the deceased.

It is further urged that deceased Thippeswamy was head of the family and out of his earnings, the entire family was maintaining, he was hale and healthy at the time of accident and because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally.
It is contended that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving by the drivers of bus, as such all the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.

3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 to 4 appeared before the court through their counsel,
but the respondent No.2 and 4 have filed written statements.

It has denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the said bus and contended that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the bus bearing Reg. No.KA-19-AD-5259 .
Further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that on 11.05.2023 at about 6.45 p.m., when the deceased was proceeding as passenger in bus bearing Reg. No.KA-19-AD- 5259, on NH-69, i.e. on Shivamogga to Sagar road, near Kumadwathi bridge, Shivamogga taluk &
district, at that time, the driver of the said bus drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against another bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07- B-3076 which was coming from opposite direction and caused the accident, due to which deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries?
2) Whether the petitioners proves that they are the legal heirs of deceased Thippeswamy ?

3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ? If so, to what extent and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?

 REASONS 10. Issue No.1:
The petitioners claim that, petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children and petitioners No.4 and 5 are the mother and father of the deceased.

To prove the same,
petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of his chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
On perusal of documents of Aadhar cards and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representative of the deceased.

However, during the pendency of the case,
the petitioner No.5 died on 28.11.2024.
Therefore, petitioners No.1 to 4 are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers to issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:
As this issue clinches the whole dispute in controversy, this issue is taken for discussion at the inception for better appreciation of evidence and dissection of materials placed on record.
The petitioners have knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation on account of death of one Thippeswamy in a Road Traffic Accident.

The first question to be considered is with regard to the negligence.
Before analyzing the factum of alleged negligence it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to the negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/heis expected to do as he/hehas some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of Jayamma vs Karthik.R.Uttarkar on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190665684/
6
human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
16. However, from the evidence placed on record it is crystal clear that, there is no qualm with the fact that, deceased breathed his last in RTA.
The only dispute in controversy is as to the alleged rash and negligent act of the offending vehicles.

17. In the instant case on hand, the petitioners in order to prove rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the bus bearing No. KA-19-D-7089 has produced police documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.
Ex.P.1 FIR and Ex.P.2 complaint.

On perusal of the FIR and complaint, these records reflects that the deceased was traveling in the private bus bearing No. KA-19-D-708 as a passenger and the driver of the private bus drove the same in rash and negligent manner and to over take another bus without observing opposite side vehicles on road, went to extreme right side and dashed to the opposite Bus.

This categorically reflects the negligence on the part of the driver of private bus bearing No. KA- 19-AD-5259.
18.
Further, the document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 and P4 being the Spot Mahazar and Sketch prepared at the time of mahazar.

Further more, the contents of Ex.P3 discloses that the road is NH-69 which is 35 feet in width, the driver of the private bus bearing No.
KA-19-AD-5259 drove his bus towards Shivamogga near Kumadvathi Bridge came extreme right side of the road without observing the vehicles on the road from opposite side and dashed against the bus bearing No.KA-07- B-3076 which came form opposite.
19.

Another important aspect this court does not loose sight of the fact that the accident had occurred only due to negligent act of the driver of the private bus bearing No. KA-19-AD-5259, if the driver of the said bus drove his vehicle with due care and cautiously in slow manner by observing ongoing vehicles on the road, he could be avoiding the accident but he has not taken cautious.
20. Even the chargesheet was also filed as against the driver of the private bus bearing No KA-19-AD-5259.
This court is aware of the fact that chargesheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.

But having regard to the Ex.P.3 and 4 which is read in consonance with the Ex.P.8 Chargesheet, it is crystal clear that there was rash and negligent act of the driver of the bus bearing No. KA-19-AD-5259.

When such is the case in the light of evidence of PW.1 and compared with police documents categorically reflects as to the rashness and negligence on the part of driver of the bus bearing No. KA-19-AD- 5259.
21.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

22. Though PW.1 was cross-examined at length by the respondent No.2 and 4 but she withstood the rigor of cross- examination.

In the instant case having regard to the other materials placed on record and other surrounding circumstances it is it is clearly forthcoming that the negligence on the part of the driver of the bus bearing No. KA-19-AD-5259.
Consequently this tribunal hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of private bus bearing No.KA-19-AD-5259.
As such, I answer Issue No.2 as in the Affirmative.

23. Issue No.3: While answering issue No.2, I have already observed that the death of Thippeswamy,
was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending private bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-19-AD-5259.
In this case, the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.75,00,000/- on the death of deceased Thippeswamy in the road traffic accident.
The petitioners contended that, deceased was an agriculturist cum Sheep farmer and also doing sheep business and earning of Rs.50,000/-p.m.
To prove the income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.
24. Be that as it may, in the absence of authentic proof of income of the deceased, this Tribunal has to consider his income notionally for calculating the compensation.
Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2023.
It is trite law that, when the petitioners have failed to prove the income, the income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
25. The next moot question to be considered is as to how the notional income has to be considered in the eye of law.
It is settled law that in case when the claimants failed to prove the income of deceased then court must dwell into take notional income.
It is relevant to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023.

entities.text: Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.

The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the Jayamma vs Karthik.R.Uttarkar on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190665684/
8
accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 11.05.2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.
26. The petitioners have produced the Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P20.

The contents ingrained in the said documents of the deceased discloses the date of birth as 01.01.1978 and the accident had taken place on 11.05.2023 and it shows that, at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 45 years.

Hence the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '14'.
27.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provided the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 45 years.
Therefore, in this case, 25% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

After adding 25% to the income of the deceased, it comes to Rs.20,000/- p.m.
(Rs.16,000x25/100=4,000+16,000).
28.
The deceased died leaving behind 4 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/4th of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.15,000/- p.m.(20000-5000 = Rs.15,000/-).
29. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.15,000/- p.m. and the multiplier '14' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.25,20,000/- (Rs.15,000 X 12 X 14).

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.25,20,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.

30. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

In this case, the petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children, petitioners No.4 is the mother of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of children/father/mother as the case may be.

As regard the apportionment of compensation is concerned, it is not in dispute that the petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 are children, petitioners No.4 is the mother of the deceased.
Hence out of the total compensation, the petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 40:15:15:30 respectively.
34. The petitioners are claiming interest @ 9% per annum on the compensation amount.
The respondent has denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

It is not in dispute that 1 st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, the 1st and 2nd respondents being the owner and insurer of the offending bus bearing Reg. No. KA-19-AD-5259 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
However the 2nd respondent being the Insurer of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-19-AD-5259 shall indemnify the 1 st respondent in payment of compensation amount to the petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
36. Issue No.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms:
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.27,29,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 40% Petitioner No.2 - 15% Petitioner No.3 - 15% Petitioner No.4 - 30% Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 to 4 a sum equal to 30% shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 70% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of Jayamma vs Karthik.R.Uttarkar on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190665684/
6
Another important aspect this court does not loose sight of the fact that the accident had occurred only due to negligent act of the driver of the private bus bearing No. KA-19-AD-5259, if the driver of the said bus drove his vehicle with due care and cautiously in slow manner by observing ongoing vehicles on the road, he could be avoiding the accident but he has not taken cautious.
This court is aware of the fact that chargesheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.
But having regard to the Ex.P.3 and 4 which is read in consonance with the Ex.P.8 Chargesheet, it is crystal clear that there was rash and negligent act of the driver of the bus bearing No. KA-19-AD-5259.
When such is the case in the light of evidence of PW.1 and compared with police documents categorically reflects as to the rashness and negligence on the part of driver of the bus bearing No. KA-19-AD- 5259.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a Jayamma vs Karthik.R.Uttarkar on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190665684/
7
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
In the instant case having regard to the other materials placed on record and other surrounding circumstances it is it is clearly forthcoming that the negligence on the part of the driver of the bus bearing No. KA-19-AD-5259.
Consequently this tribunal hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of private bus bearing No.KA-19-AD-5259.
In this case, the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.75,00,000/- on the death of deceased Thippeswamy in the road traffic accident.
To prove the income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.
Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2023.
It is trite law that, when the petitioners have failed to prove the income, the income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
It is settled law that in case when the claimants failed to prove the income of deceased then court must dwell into take notional income.
As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.
In this case, the petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children, petitioners No.4 is the mother of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of children/father/mother as the case may be.
The respondents have not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.25,20,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.
Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
Therefore, the 1st and 2nd respondents being the owner and insurer of the offending bus bearing Reg. No. KA-19-AD-5259 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
However the 2nd respondent being the Insurer of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-19-AD-5259 shall indemnify the 1 st respondent in payment of compensation amount to the petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
36. Issue No.4 :
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms:
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.27,29,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 40% Petitioner No.2 - 15% Petitioner No.3 - 15% Petitioner No.4 - 30% Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 to 4 a sum equal to 30% shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 70% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
